question: A silicon diode starts conducting appreciably when the forward bias is about $0.7\text{ V}$. If it is connected in series with a $500\Omega$ resistor across a $5\text{ V}$ supply, estimate the current through the circuit after conduction begins.

options.A: After conduction begins, resistor voltage is $5-0.7=4.3\text{ V}$. Hence $I=\dfrac{4.3}{500}=8.6\times10^{-3}\text{ A}=8.6\text{ mA}$.
options.B: $I=\dfrac{5}{500}=10\text{ mA}$ because the diode voltage drop is ignored.
options.C: $I=\dfrac{0.7}{500}=1.4\text{ mA}$ because the resistor gets only the diode voltage.
options.D: $I=\dfrac{5+0.7}{500}=11.4\text{ mA}$ because diode voltage adds to the supply.
